name: dfu-util
why: USB device firmware upgrade tool; a door into flashing boards and poking at USB DFU mode, though fairly standard hardware plumbing.

brief.what_it_is: dfu-util is a host-side implementation of the USB Forum's DFU 1.0 and DFU 1.1 (Device Firmware Upgrade) specifications. It downloads firmware to a DFU-enabled USB device or uploads firmware from one. Targets range from small microcontroller boards to mobile phones. The package also ships dfu-suffix, which adds, checks, or removes a DFU firmware file suffix, and dfu-prefix, which works with TI LMDFU/Stellaris and NXP LPC file formats.
brief.why_it_exists: DFU is the USB standard for loading firmware onto devices, and the homepage presents dfu-util as the host-side tool for doing that across many boards and phones. The suffix tool exists so a firmware file can be safely matched to a device before flashing.
brief.how_it_works: dfu-util uses libusb 1.0 to talk to the device over USB. On Windows, the device has to be registered with the WinUSB driver (libusb-win32 or libusbK are listed as alternatives). The homepage says the Stellaris/LPC prefix formats are handled by dfu-prefix and the suffix check by dfu-suffix.

commands_seen.context: Homepage's install route for Mac OS X users via Homebrew (the same command this catalogue entry is based on).
Homepage's way to clone the development Git repository before building from source.

brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install: Homebrew and MacPorts are listed for Mac OS X. Most Linux distributions package it; Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora and Gentoo are named, and OpenSuSe, Mandriva and CentOS packages come from the Open Build Service. Windows binaries are offered, but the device must be registered with the WinUSB driver (or libusb-win32/libusbK) through the libusb wiki's instructions. Building from source uses the project's build instructions page, which I did not open. No accounts or runtimes are mentioned.
brief.standout: One tool covers a wide range of hardware, from Openmoko phones to STM32 boards, Black Magic Probe, and Particle devices, through ST's DfuSe extension. The dfu-suffix step adds a file-to-device matching check before flashing, which many quick flashing tools skip.
brief.status: Maintained, as far as the homepage shows. It lists 0.11 as the current release, and the copyright line reads 2010-2025 with Tormod Volden named as maintainer. No release date or last commit date was visible, so the exact recency is unknown.
brief.caveats: Windows users have to swap the device driver to WinUSB, libusb-win32, or libusbK before it works. The homepage says the Qi Hardware ATUSB needs dfu-util 0.7 specifically, not the current release. The homepage points to a manual page for examples, but I did not fetch it, so no usage beyond the two commands above is verified here. Licensed under GPL version 2.
quotes: dfu-util is a host side implementation of the DFU 1.0 and DFU 1.1 specifications of the USB forum.
DFU is intended to download and upload firmware to/from devices connected over USB.
Mac OS X users can also get dfu-util from Homebrew with "brew install dfu-util" or from MacPorts.
